children: The project adds to Bondada Engineering’s growing power-infrastructure portfolio as India accelerates smart metering to improve discom efficiency and financial sustainability

India’s smart metering push is creating a growing order pipeline for power-infrastructure companies, with Bondada Engineering securing a Rs 410 million project in Telangana through a joint venture. The order strengthens the company’s presence in the electricity distribution segment as states step up investments in digital grid infrastructure.The project comes amid a broader government-led drive to modernise India’s distribution network.

Under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), smart metering works have been sanctioned across 28 states and Union Territories, covering 197.9 million consumers, 5.253 million distribution transformers and 205,000 feeders. As of March 2026, 61.3 million smart meters had been installed across the country under various schemes.

The Telangana order highlights the business opportunity emerging from the shift towards technology-led power distribution. Smart meters enable utilities to monitor consumption more closely, improve billing and collections, reduce commercial losses and strengthen cash flows. Government data shows that aggregate technical and commercial losses across utilities improved from 21.91 per cent in FY2021 to 15.04 per cent in FY2025, with smart metering among the measures supporting distribution-sector reforms. Industry experts say continued deployment of smart meters is likely to support demand for engineering, procurement, installation and digital monitoring services, while creating recurring opportunities around grid modernisation.

For engineering companies, smart metering is increasingly becoming part of the wider power-infrastructure investment cycle alongside renewable integration, transmission upgrades and grid digitisation. The RDSS, launched in 2021, has an approved outlay of Rs 3.03 trillion, underlining the scale of capital being directed towards improving distribution infrastructure.

The latest order therefore gives Bondada Engineering exposure to a segment where policy support, rising electricity demand and the need for financially stronger distribution companies are converging. The expansion of smart infrastructure could also help utilities integrate distributed renewable generation and manage electricity demand more efficiently.
